label: Pass data between steps with data pills
description: Learn how ByteChef steps share data. A Variable step holds a name and a city, a Text Helper step upper-cases the city, and a Logger step combines both into a greeting using data pills such as ${var_1.name}. It runs with one click and needs no connection.

tasks.label: Set name and city
tasks.name: var_1
tasks.description: Holds an object with a name and a city. Its output is that object, so later steps can use ${var_1.name} and ${var_1.city}.

tasks.label: Make the city upper case
tasks.name: textHelper_1
tasks.description: Takes the city from the first step with the ${var_1.city} data pill and returns it in capital letters. Its whole output is used as ${textHelper_1}.

tasks.label: Log a greeting
tasks.name: logger_1
tasks.description: Writes a greeting to the execution log, built from two data pills: ${var_1.name} from the first step and ${textHelper_1} from the second.

stickyNotes.content:
## Start here: pass data between steps

Every step can use what earlier steps returned. You pick it as a **data pill**, which is written as `${step_name.field}`. This workflow needs no connection.

1. Click **Test** at the top to run it.
2. Click **Set name and city** and open its **Output** tab: it returned `name` and `city`.
3. Click **Make the city upper case**. Its text is `${var_1.city}`, the city from step 1, and its output is the same city in capitals.
4. Click **Log a greeting**. Its text mixes plain words with two pills: `${var_1.name}` and `${textHelper_1}`. Open **Logs** after a run to read the result.
5. Change the name in **Set name and city** to your own and click **Test** again.
6. Optional: open **Workflow Inputs** in the right sidebar, add an input called `name` and set a test value for it. Then replace `${var_1.name}` with `${name}` in **Log a greeting** and click **Test**.
